spec.title: Air quality — Sensor.Community, live
spec.description: Particulate matter from Sensor.Community's citizen sensors, worldwide, reloaded every 5 minutes.

source.sql:
-- One row per outdoor sensor that measures particulate matter: its 24-hour
-- mean and, when it reported in the last 5 minutes, its latest reading.
-- P2 is PM2.5 and P1 is PM10, in µg/m³. Readings outside 0-500 µg/m³ are left
-- out: a low-cost sensor in fog, or with a failing fan, reports thousands.
WITH day AS (
  SELECT
    r.sensor.id AS sensor_id,
    any_value(r.sensor.sensor_type.name) AS sensor_type,
    any_value(r.location.country) AS country,
    any_value(r.location.latitude::DOUBLE) AS latitude,
    any_value(r.location.longitude::DOUBLE) AS longitude,
    avg(try_cast(list_filter(r.sensordatavalues, lambda x: x.value_type = 'P2')[1].value AS DOUBLE)) AS pm25_24h,
    avg(try_cast(list_filter(r.sensordatavalues, lambda x: x.value_type = 'P1')[1].value AS DOUBLE)) AS pm10_24h
  FROM read_json('https://data.sensor.community/static/v2/data.24h.json') AS r
  WHERE r.location.indoor::INTEGER = 0
  GROUP BY 1
),
now AS (
  SELECT
    r.sensor.id AS sensor_id,
    max(r.timestamp::TIMESTAMP AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS time,
    avg(try_cast(list_filter(r.sensordatavalues, lambda x: x.value_type = 'P2')[1].value AS DOUBLE)) AS pm25_now,
    avg(try_cast(list_filter(r.sensordatavalues, lambda x: x.value_type = 'P1')[1].value AS DOUBLE)) AS pm10_now
  FROM read_json('https://data.sensor.community/static/v2/data.dust.min.json') AS r
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  d.sensor_id, d.sensor_type, d.country, d.latitude, d.longitude,
  round(d.pm25_24h, 1) AS pm25_24h,
  round(d.pm10_24h, 1) AS pm10_24h,
  n.time,
  round(CASE WHEN n.pm25_now BETWEEN 0 AND 500 THEN n.pm25_now END, 1) AS pm25_now,
  round(CASE WHEN n.pm10_now BETWEEN 0 AND 500 THEN n.pm10_now END, 1) AS pm10_now
FROM day AS d LEFT JOIN now AS n USING (sensor_id)
WHERE d.pm25_24h BETWEEN 0 AND 500
  AND d.latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90 AND d.longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180
  AND NOT (d.latitude = 0 AND d.longitude = 0)

SELECT f.properties.ISO_A2_EH::VARCHAR AS code, f.properties.NAME_EN::VARCHAR AS name
FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/v5.1.2/geojson/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.geojson'), unnest(features) AS t(f)
WHERE f.properties.ISO_A2_EH::VARCHAR <> '-99'

spec.sql:
-- Value first, text second: the ISO code filters, the name shows.
SELECT s.country, any_value(coalesce(n.name, s.country)) AS name
FROM $sensors AS s LEFT JOIN $names AS n ON n.code = s.country
GROUP BY s.country
ORDER BY name

-- Spread over the countries picked: their sensors' extent is cut into a
-- 6 x 6 grid, and the cards go to the most polluted sensor of each cell
-- first, then the second of each, and so on up to 20. The 20 most polluted
-- alone tend to sit in one city, card over card.
WITH c AS (
  SELECT sensor_id, sensor_type, latitude, longitude, pm25_24h FROM $sensors
  WHERE NOT '__all__' IN ($country) AND country IN ($country) AND pm25_now IS NOT NULL
),
grid AS (
  SELECT greatest(max(latitude) - min(latitude), max(longitude) - min(longitude), 0.1) / 6 AS size FROM c
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT c.*, row_number() OVER (
    PARTITION BY floor(latitude / grid.size), floor(longitude / grid.size) ORDER BY pm25_24h DESC) AS rk
  FROM c, grid
)
SELECT f FROM (
  SELECT lower(sensor_type) || '_sensor_' || sensor_id AS f FROM ranked
  ORDER BY rk, pm25_24h DESC LIMIT 20
)
UNION
SELECT lower(sensor_type) || '_sensor_' || sensor_id FROM $sensors WHERE sensor_id::VARCHAR = $sensor

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: each sensor's readings over the days picked in the time range,
-- from Sensor.Community's archive, one CSV per sensor and day, published the
-- day after. Read through the gateway's cache (feeds), and with http_get, which
-- leaves out a day a sensor did not report (404) instead of failing the query.
-- At most 7 days, never today (not archived yet). The columns differ by sensor
-- type, so PM2.5 (P2) is found by name in each file's header. Half-hour means.
WITH files AS (
  SELECT f, strftime(d, '%Y-%m-%d') AS day
  -- Cast: with no sensor picked the list is empty, and an empty list has no type.
  FROM unnest(CAST([${spark:singlequote}] AS VARCHAR[])) AS s(f),
       unnest(generate_series(
         greatest(DATE '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD}', DATE '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD}' - INTERVAL 6 DAY),
         least(DATE '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD}', current_date - 1),
         INTERVAL 1 DAY)) AS t(d)
  WHERE f LIKE '%_sensor_%'
),
fetched AS (
  SELECT http_get('http://feeds/sensor-community/archive/' || day || '/' || day || '_' || f || '.csv') AS r FROM files
),
lines AS (
  SELECT string_split(trim(r->>'body'), chr(10)) AS l FROM fetched WHERE (r->>'status') = '200'
),
cells AS (
  SELECT list_position(string_split(l[1], ';'), 'P2') AS i, string_split(unnest(l[2:]), ';') AS c FROM lines
)
SELECT 'Sensor ' || c[1] AS name, c[1] AS sensor_id,
       any_value(c[4]::DOUBLE) AS latitude, any_value(c[5]::DOUBLE) AS longitude,
       time_bucket(INTERVAL 30 MINUTE, c[6]::TIMESTAMP) AS time,
       round(avg(try_cast(c[i] AS DOUBLE)) FILTER (WHERE try_cast(c[i] AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 0 AND 500), 1) AS pm25
FROM cells
WHERE len(c) >= 6 AND c[1] <> ''
GROUP BY c[1], time_bucket(INTERVAL 30 MINUTE, c[6]::TIMESTAMP)
ORDER BY sensor_id, time

spec.title: Sensors
spec.description: Outdoor sensors with a 24-hour PM2.5 mean, within the area, country and range selected.

spec.rawSql:
WITH area AS (
  SELECT list_transform(xs, lambda x: x - 360 * round(coalesce(list_avg(xs), 0) / 360)) AS xs, ys
  FROM (
    SELECT
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
    FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($area, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
  )
)
SELECT count(*) AS "Sensors"
FROM $sensors, area
WHERE (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
  AND ('__all__' IN ($country) OR country IN ($country))
  AND least(pm25_24h, 99.9) >= coalesce(try_cast($pm_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
  AND least(pm25_24h, 99.9) < coalesce(try_cast($pm_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE)

spec.title: Meet WHO
spec.description: Share of sensors whose 24-hour PM2.5 mean is at or under 15 µg/m³, the WHO 2021 air quality guideline.

spec.rawSql:
WITH area AS (
  SELECT list_transform(xs, lambda x: x - 360 * round(coalesce(list_avg(xs), 0) / 360)) AS xs, ys
  FROM (
    SELECT
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
    FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($area, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
  )
)
SELECT avg(CASE WHEN pm25_24h <= 15 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS "Meet WHO"
FROM $sensors, area
WHERE (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
  AND ('__all__' IN ($country) OR country IN ($country))
  AND least(pm25_24h, 99.9) >= coalesce(try_cast($pm_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
  AND least(pm25_24h, 99.9) < coalesce(try_cast($pm_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE)

spec.title: WHO bands
spec.description: Sensors per WHO 2021 band of 24-hour PM2.5, in the map's colours. Click a band to filter the dashboard to it; click it again to clear.

spec.rawSql:
WITH area AS (
  SELECT list_transform(xs, lambda x: x - 360 * round(coalesce(list_avg(xs), 0) / 360)) AS xs, ys
  FROM (
    SELECT
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
    FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($area, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
  )
)
-- Selected: $pm_lo to $pm_hi
SELECT CASE WHEN pm25_24h <= 15 THEN 0 WHEN pm25_24h <= 25 THEN 1 WHEN pm25_24h <= 37.5 THEN 2 WHEN pm25_24h <= 50 THEN 3 WHEN pm25_24h <= 75 THEN 4 ELSE 5 END AS band,
       count(*) AS n
FROM $sensors, area
WHERE (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
  AND ('__all__' IN ($country) OR country IN ($country))
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

spec.title: PM2.5, 24-hour mean
spec.description: Drag across the bars to filter the dashboard by 24-hour PM2.5. Grey is every sensor; colour is what the area and country leave. 100 µg/m³ or more falls in the last bar.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT floor(least(pm25_24h, 99.9) / 5) * 5 AS bin, count(*) AS n
FROM $sensors
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH area AS (
  SELECT list_transform(xs, lambda x: x - 360 * round(coalesce(list_avg(xs), 0) / 360)) AS xs, ys
  FROM (
    SELECT

    FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($area, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
  )
)
SELECT floor(least(pm25_24h, 99.9) / 5) * 5 AS bin, count(*) AS n
FROM $sensors, area
WHERE (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
  AND ('__all__' IN ($country) OR country IN ($country))
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

spec.title: Countries by median PM2.5
spec.description: The 25 countries with the highest median 24-hour PM2.5, among those with at least 5 sensors in the area drawn. Click a bar to filter the dashboard to that country, and to draw its interpolated surface on the map; click it again to clear.

spec.rawSql:
WITH area AS (
  SELECT list_transform(xs, lambda x: x - 360 * round(coalesce(list_avg(xs), 0) / 360)) AS xs, ys
  FROM (
    SELECT
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
    FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($area, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
  )
)
-- Selected: $country
SELECT country, count(*) AS sensors, median(pm25_24h) AS median
FROM $sensors, area
WHERE (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
GROUP BY country
HAVING count(*) >= 5
ORDER BY median DESC
LIMIT 25

spec.title: PM2.5 by sensor and country
spec.description: Every outdoor Sensor.Community sensor, over each country's median, in the WHO 2021 bands of 24-hour PM2.5: at or under 15 µg/m³ meets the guideline; 25, 37.5, 50 and 75 are its interim targets. Choose a country (click its bar) to draw an interpolated surface of it, up to 25 km from any sensor. Click a country to pick it in the Country picker; click a sensor to see its readings; draw an area to filter the rest of the dashboard.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT sensor_id, sensor_type, country, latitude, longitude, pm25_24h, pm10_24h, pm25_now, pm10_now, time
FROM $sensors
WHERE ('__all__' IN ($country) OR country IN ($country))
  AND least(pm25_24h, 99.9) >= coalesce(try_cast($pm_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
  AND least(pm25_24h, 99.9) < coalesce(try_cast($pm_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE)

SELECT country, median(pm25_24h) AS avg_pm25
FROM $sensors
GROUP BY country
HAVING count(*) >= 5

SELECT latitude, longitude, pm25_24h
FROM $sensors
WHERE NOT '__all__' IN ($country) AND country IN ($country)

spec.title: PM2.5 over the days picked
spec.description: Half-hour PM2.5 of the sensors with a card on the map (20 spread over the countries picked, the most polluted of each part first, and the one clicked), in grey, with their median in orange. The dashed line is the WHO 2021 guideline, 15 µg/m³, which is set for a 24-hour mean. The time range picks the days; the archive ends yesterday. The crosshair is shared: hover here and the map's cards show the same moment.

spec.rawSql: SELECT time, name, pm25 FROM $archive ORDER BY time
SELECT time, median(pm25) AS pm25 FROM $archive GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

SELECT sensor_id AS "Sensor", country AS "Country", sensor_type AS "Type",
       round(latitude, 3) AS "Latitude", round(longitude, 3) AS "Longitude",
       pm25_24h AS "PM2.5, 24 h", pm10_24h AS "PM10, 24 h",
       pm25_now AS "PM2.5, now", pm10_now AS "PM10, now",
       coalesce(strftime(time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', '%H:%M UTC'), 'not in the last 5 min') AS "Last reading"
FROM $sensors
WHERE sensor_id::VARCHAR = $sensor

options.content:
**Pick countries** at the top, **click a country** on the map, or **click its bar**. **Click a sensor** on the map to see its readings and a card with its last days. Picking countries zooms the figures to them, draws their interpolated surface, and puts up cards for 20 of their sensors, spread over them, the most polluted of each part first. The **time range** picks the days the cards show.

**Click a WHO band**, **drag** across the PM2.5 bars or **draw** an area on the map: every panel follows, answered in your browser. The data reloads every 5 minutes.

### Where the data comes from

[Sensor.Community](https://sensor.community/) (formerly Luftdaten) is a citizen science network: volunteers build low-cost particulate matter sensors, most of them the Nova SDS011, and hang them outside their windows. Each sensor sends a reading every few minutes, and the network publishes them [as open data](https://github.com/opendata-stuttgart/meta/wiki/EN-APIs) under the [Open Database License (ODbL 1.0)](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/).

This dashboard reads two of its files, straight from your browser:

- **`data.24h.json`**: each sensor's mean over the last 24 hours. The map, the histogram and the figures use it.
- **`data.dust.min.json`**: the last 5 minutes. *Live now* and a sensor's *now* columns come from it.

Both are refreshed by Sensor.Community every few minutes, and the dashboard reloads them every 5 minutes.

The sparkline cards on the map come from a third source, the [archive](https://archive.sensor.community/): one file per sensor and day, with a reading every few minutes, shown here as half-hour means. The archive is published the day after, so the cards never reach today; the time range picks their days (up to 7). These files are read by Grafana's server, through a cache, since a missing day would otherwise fail the whole query.

### How to read it

- **PM2.5** and **PM10** are the mass of airborne particles under 2.5 and 10 micrometres across, in µg/m³.
- The colours are the [WHO 2021 air quality guidelines](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240034228) for PM2.5 over 24 hours: **15 µg/m³** is the guideline; 25, 37.5, 50 and 75 are its interim targets. The guideline is set for a 24-hour mean, which is why the map is coloured by it rather than by the last 5 minutes.
- These are **low-cost sensors, uncorrected**. Their optical counters read high in humid air and fog, and drift with age; no reading here is a regulatory measurement. Read the map for patterns across many sensors, not for one sensor's exact value.
- Indoor sensors are left out, and so are readings outside 0–500 µg/m³ (a failing sensor can report thousands).

### The map

Three layers, in the same colours: each sensor; under them, each country's median sensor (countries with at least 5); and, once a country is chosen, a surface interpolated between its sensors (inverse distance weighting, up to 25 km from the nearest one). The surface fills the gaps between sensors with a guess, not a measurement: where they are sparse, trust it less.

### How it works

Both files are loaded into DuckDB running in your browser (the Chaski data source). Every filter and click is answered there, without a round trip to the server. The map is the Kepler Geospatial Maps Plus panel, which places the countries and draws the surface; the charts are Business Charts (Apache ECharts).
